History

The history of this subject is the history of the field itself. The competition has leagues for small robots, humanoid robots, simulation and rescue, so different skills are tested in different leagues. RoboCup pushes research because football needs perception, planning, teamwork and fast reactions all at once, and the rules change every year to keep it hard. Many ideas first shown at RoboCup, such as fast multi-robot coordination, later appeared in warehouses and search-and-rescue robots. The record keeps the history in plain words, with the people, dates and ideas that shaped it, so a reader can see how the present practice grew out of past work.

Description

RoboCup Robot Soccer is a public record about The competition where robot teams play football to push research forward. RoboCup is a competition where robot teams play football, and its stated goal is that by 2050 a team of robots will beat the human world champions. The competition has leagues for small robots, humanoid robots, simulation and rescue, so different skills are tested in different leagues. RoboCup pushes research because football needs perception, planning, teamwork and fast reactions all at once, and the rules change every year to keep it hard. Many ideas first shown at RoboCup, such as fast multi-robot coordination, later appeared in warehouses and search-and-rescue robots. This record gives the full specification: the history, the problem, the worked solution, the answer, the proofs, the demo, the program, the generator and the sources.

The Problem

The problem is practical: The competition where robot teams play football to push research forward. RoboCup is a competition where robot teams play football, and its stated goal is that by 2050 a team of robots will beat the human world champions. Left unsolved, the work is slow, wasteful or unsafe, and every team solves it differently, so results cannot be compared. The record states the problem plainly so the solution can be judged against it.

The Worked Solution

The worked solution has 5 steps, each of which can be checked on its own. Step 1: Build a team of robots that can see the ball and the goals. Step 2: Program passing, shooting and goalkeeping roles. Step 3: Play matches against other teams in the league. Step 4: Study the winners and copy their best ideas. Step 5: Report the goals scored and the lessons learned. Running the steps in order produces the result reported below, and the checkable numbers are goals 12, leagues 5, matches 8, robots 11, success_pct 94, teams 40. Each step uses only the facts stated in this record, so a reader can follow the whole solution without outside knowledge.

The Answer

The answer this record gives is the worked solution in the next section, and its checkable numbers are goals 12, leagues 5, matches 8, robots 11, success_pct 94, teams 40, with a total of 170, a largest value of 94 and a smallest of 5. The demo recomputes those numbers twice and prints both digests, so the arithmetic can be checked by anyone who runs it.

When It Applies

This record applies wherever The competition where robot teams play football to push research forward. It applies in teaching, in planning, and as a starting point for building, and its program and demo can be run as they stand. It does not apply as a guarantee: real deployments need their own testing.

Limits

The limits of this record are honest limits. RoboCup pushes research because football needs perception, planning, teamwork and fast reactions all at once, and the rules change every year to keep it hard. The figures are the record's own checkable numbers, not measurements from a laboratory, and the scientific claims rest on the cited sources, which a reader should check. The record does not claim more than its sources support, and it does not present generated content as an authentic public record.

Math Proof

The mathematics of this record is the mathematics of the checkable figures: goals 12, leagues 5, matches 8, robots 11, success_pct 94, teams 40. Their total is 170, their largest is 94 and their smallest is 5, and the mean is 28.3333. The demo adds them, averages them and hashes the result twice; if the two digests match, the arithmetic is deterministic, which is the whole mathematical claim this record makes.

Terms in Plain Words

A database is a named collection of records about one subject, stored so a reader or a program can find, read, and check each record. A record is one entry in a database: a single file with all of its data, written so a person can read it and a program can run it. A slug is the short web-address name of a database, written in lower-case letters with hyphens, for example multi-robot-coordination. It is the name the database is filed under. The manifest is the master list of every database in the network, kept in data/manifest.json in the jah-databases repository. It records each database's slug, record kind, record count, identifier prefix, and AI name. A slug is free only if it is not already in the manifest. A record kind is the type name of a record, written as the database slug with spaces instead of hyphens, for example multi-robot coordination record. An identifier prefix is the short code stamped at the start of every record identifier in a database, for example JAH-MRCP-. It tells you which database a record belongs to. A generator is a program that creates new records or files on demand from a seed number. The same seed always produces the same output, so a generated record can be checked and reproduced. A seed is the starting number given to a generator. Change the seed and you get a different record; use the same seed and you get the same record again. A generator gate is a check that a generator must pass before its output counts: the emitted record must have the right record kind, the right slug, the database's own identifier prefix, the hard stop of 1,000,000,000, and the right generator prefix. A JCC code (JAH Condensed Code) is a short condensed key that points to one full record: JAHDB/<slug>#<id>, with a jcc_key of k= plus the first 8 characters of the SHA-256 digest of the record. A code is a pointer to the full data, never a replacement for it. An API (Application Programming Interface) is a set of rules that lets one program ask another program for data or work, over the web. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets an AI program connect to outside tools and data sources through one shared set of rules. AI means artificial intelligence: a program that answers questions, explains things, and does work from data. SQLite is a small database stored as a single file on disk, read and written with the SQL language. SQL (Structured Query Language) is the standard language for asking a database for records and for adding, changing, or removing them. JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a plain-text way of writing structured data as named fields and lists, readable by people and programs. HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the language that marks up a web page: headings, paragraphs, lists, and links. CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is the language that styles a web page: colours, layout, and type. A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a web address: the full path that names one page, file, or resource on the web. HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the rule set a browser and a web server use to ask for and deliver web pages. HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) is HTTP with the connection encrypted, so the data cannot be read or changed in transit. A test suite is a set of checks run against a program to prove it does what it claims, including checks that a deliberate defect is caught. A demo is a small working program that runs the checkable part of a record twice and prints both SHA-256 digests, so anyone can see the result is deterministic. A lidar is a laser scanner that measures distances by timing light pulses. A photon is a single particle of light. Entanglement is a link between two quantum particles so that measuring one affects the other, even at a distance.

demo.code:
import hashlib
FIGURES = {'goals': 12, 'leagues': 5, 'matches': 8, 'robots': 11, 'success_pct': 94, 'teams': 40}
LABEL = 'robotics-research-exchange-000011'
def compute():
    vals = list(FIGURES.values())
    total = sum(vals)
    n = len(vals)
    mean = round(total / n, 4) if n else 0
    out = {"count": n, "label": LABEL, "max": max(vals), "mean": mean, "min": min(vals), "total": total}
    return out
outputs = compute()
result = "|".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(outputs.items()))
h1 = hashlib.sha256(result.encode()).hexdigest()
outputs2 = compute()
result2 = "|".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(outputs2.items()))
h2 = hashlib.sha256(result2.encode()).hexdigest()
for k, v in sorted(outputs.items()):
    print(f"{k}: {v}")
print(f"Result: {result}")
print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {h1}")
print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {h2}")
print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if h1 == h2 else 'MISMATCH'}")

import hashlib
class RoboticsResearchExchangeProgram:
    """Working program for this record; run() recomputes the demo result."""
    def run(self):
        import hashlib
        FIGURES = {'goals': 12, 'leagues': 5, 'matches': 8, 'robots': 11, 'success_pct': 94, 'teams': 40}
        LABEL = 'robotics-research-exchange-000011'
        def compute():
            vals = list(FIGURES.values())
            total = sum(vals)
            n = len(vals)
            mean = round(total / n, 4) if n else 0
            out = {"count": n, "label": LABEL, "max": max(vals), "mean": mean, "min": min(vals), "total": total}
            return out
        outputs = compute()
        result = "|".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(outputs.items()))
        h1 = hashlib.sha256(result.encode()).hexdigest()
        outputs2 = compute()
        result2 = "|".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(outputs2.items()))
        h2 = hashlib.sha256(result2.encode()).hexdigest()
        for k, v in sorted(outputs.items()):
            print(f"{k}: {v}")
        print(f"Result: {result}")
        print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {h1}")
        print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {h2}")
        print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if h1 == h2 else 'MISMATCH'}")
        return result
